text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Sabah Chief Minister Yong Teck Lee said the impending peace in the southern Philippines would have great significance in Sabah, especially in finding a solution to the problem of the large Filipino illegal immigrant population in the state.

- The Gerakan power tussle took a twist yesterday when the High Court clarified that its orders granted to Batu member of parliament Joseph Chong were only to ensure that he was allowed to file his nomination papers. Chong is battling for leadership of the party.
- Tenaga Nasional Bhd operations may be broken up into three areas -- generation, transmission and distribution -- under a proposed restructuring by executive chairman Tajuddin Ali.

- The delay in signing the engineering, procurement and construction agreement for the 13.6 billion ringgit Bakun dam project between Ekran Bhd and Asea Brown Boveri was due to disagreement on the text of the contract.

- Amanah Saham Wawasan 2020 saw encouraging participation from both Bumiputera (ethnic Malay) and non-Bumiputera investors with more than 680,000 people having invested about 1.3 billion ringgit in the scheme during the one-month special offer period.
